en: For the majority of this course, we talked
about AI agents because obviously they are
the most exciting thing in that entire
space. But in reality,
you often want an AI workflow in many
situations. So just to make sure we're on
the same page,
a workflow, no matter if it uses AI or not,
by the way, is just a deterministic flow of
clearly defined actions, which means at the
point of time where you build a workflow,
not where it runs, but where you build it,
you clearly decide the sequence of steps and
what should happen in each step. And every
workflow has some trigger, some input that
activates and runs the workflow, you could
say, like a new support email arriving, for
example.
Then you have one or more steps not decided
by some model, but instead clearly decided
by you when you build it.
For example, you may summarize an email, you
may classify the topic and maybe also save
it to the database or do just one of these
things.
And then some output is typically generated,
for example, that may then maybe also have
been saved to a database.
That's the idea behind a workflow,
predictability, clearly defined steps, as
you will also see once we start building one
or once you see one in action.
